selected.title: Before the robot moves
selected.texas_link: UT Austin is awardee and Austin is performance city.

movement.action: funded a project whose period began
movement.object: UT Austin robot safety research using deep generative modeling

selected.why_today: The funded project period began five days before this edition; current NSF record retains that start date.
selected.consequence: A proposed reusable learned safety filter will be evaluated in physical robot experiments, including pick-and-place near fragile objects.
selected.application_change: The proposed filter learns from safe demonstrations rather than requiring every safety constraint to be hand-authored.
selected.counter_image: A degraded camera or locked motor joint is a planned recovery case, not a successful recovery already demonstrated.
selected.earned_take: A plausible safer move is not safety evidence; the project must compare measured failures with its claimed bounds.

agency.next_step: Physical experiments, user studies and benchmark comparisons in the funded project.
agency.who_can_act: David Fridovich-Keil and collaborators; researchers can eventually inspect the planned open-source output.

sources.title: NSF Award 2535276: Collaborative Research: Robot Safety with Deep Generative Modeling

filmability.viewer_question: Can a robot change a risky move before it carries a fragile object?
filmability.opening_action: Illustrated robot gripper carries a small block toward a glass; the proposed path would pass too close.
filmability.mechanism: Safe demonstrations supply the learned reference; a proposed action is pulled toward that reference before execution.
filmability.human_consequence: Workers near assembly or assistive robots may gain a reusable safety layer if tests support the proposed method.
filmability.source_limit: This is a funded project starting October 1st, not a measured operational safety result. An illustrative route is a conceptual example, not the actual model output.
three_key_images: Same robot, carried block and glass establish a recognizable pick-and-place task.
A clearly illustrated candidate route moves toward a safe demonstrated route before the gripper executes it.
The same unchanged glass and completed placement reveal the intended test; the close states that failure rates still need comparison.

asset_leads.relevant_image: Lab lists two seven-degree-of-freedom robot arms and links a robot photo.
asset_leads.what_it_proves: The lab reports its equipment inventory; this does not establish use for award 2535276.
asset_leads.inspection: Asset URL found on fully fetched lab equipment page; pixels were not inspected and asset is not admitted.
asset_leads.rights_basis: No explicit reuse license located in this bounded pass.

action_support.pictured_action: Illustrative gripper picks a block and a candidate path approaches a glass.
action_support.scope_fit: The abstract explicitly names pick-and-place near fragile objects; avoid brand-specific equipment or pretending to observe a test.

action_support.pictured_action: The candidate path shifts toward safe demonstration paths before the gripper travels.
action_support.scope_fit: Show a conceptual learned-action projection, not a deterministic collision sensor, shield bubble or actual algorithm output.

action_support.pictured_action: Gripper follows illustrative revised motion while glass stays untouched; close on the unproven test.
action_support.scope_fit: Intended behavior only; no accident prevented, measured success rate or workplace deployment is established.

filmability.strongest_useful_image: The gripper, block and glass stay identical while the proposed route changes before execution.
filmability.next_information: Show demonstrations as the source of the changed action, then return to the same pick-and-place task.
filmability.likely_false_inference: Viewer may think the animation depicts a deployed system that has prevented an accident.
filmability.preventive_limit: Display Illustration — proposed research throughout and state the project has just begun; tests will compare failure rates.
filmability.missing_picture: No observed current test, empirical failure rate or actual learned filter output is available. Those cannot be pictured as verified results.
filmability.implementation_status: Research proposal only. Director must bind a real module and obtain independent current code, muted phone and native proof.

visual_stakes.affected_person: People working alongside assembly and assistive robots
visual_stakes.physical_subject: Robot gripper carrying a block near a fragile glass
visual_stakes.visible_change: A proposed action changes before execution
visual_stakes.consequence: The intended test is completing a placement without disturbing the glass; safety performance remains unmeasured in this source.
visual_stakes.opening_question: Can a robot change a risky move before it carries a fragile object?
visual_stakes.answer: The proposed learned filter can change the action toward demonstrated behavior; the new research must test whether it is safer.
visual_stakes.asset_fit: Original disclosed illustration can show the source-named pick-and-place relationship without requiring synthetic human performance.

action_proposals.visible_action: An illustrated gripper carries a block beside fragile glass. A proposed path bends toward demonstrated routes before the corrected move executes.
action_proposals.consequence: A proposed reusable learned safety filter will be evaluated in physical robot experiments, including pick-and-place near fragile objects.
action_proposals.limits: Illustration of proposed research. No actual robot, learned model output, measured failure rate or proven accident prevention is depicted.
action_proposals.source_basis: The NSF abstract explicitly names pick-and-place near fragile objects and a diffusion model projecting actions toward safe expert demonstrations.

rejected.title: AI-MARRVEL and BRSK1 follow-up experiments
rejected.reason: Current and sourced, but the decisive experiment is comparing impaired and partly restored fly movement. No inspected licensed footage of these tests was available; inventing movement magnitudes or a gene-function visual would add unsupported biological detail. Robot motion projection is a more direct source-named explanatory relationship.
rejected.source_limit: Release reports a likely diagnosis; no routine clinical use or treatment outcome is established.

rejected.title: Predict-WTE wrong-tooth warning pilot
rejected.reason: Page is undated and supplies no observed extraction-warning workflow, validation or operating results. A tooth-mismatch check would be an invented algorithm detail.
